text: dsh-user-preferences 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的偏好注入插件，通过 systemPrompt 注册提示词片段，并在插件页面提供编辑界面。它读取全局 Markdown 和当前项目最近的偏好文件，组合后注入每次模型请求；用户可选择合并到系统提示词或作为独立上下文，也可设置字符预算。插件页面支持查看状态、保存全局偏好、切换启用状态与注入模式，并可导入 Claude Code 或 Codex 规则文件。另有 /preferences 命令查看状态或全局文件路径。代码未显示需要 API 密钥或外部账号。

dsh-user-preferences injects global and nearest-project Markdown preferences into DSH requests. Users choose system-prompt or separate-context mode and a character budget. Its Plugins page edits preferences and imports Claude Code or Codex rules; /preferences reports status or the global file path.
想让自己常用的规则自动带进每次 DSH 对话。
能不能给不同项目设置各自的 Markdown 偏好，并自动应用？
I want my standing instructions included in every DSH request.
dsh-user-preferences 的功能「全局与项目偏好注入」：每次请求时读取全局 Markdown 和当前目录向上查找到的项目偏好，按字符预算组合后注入。用户可选择合并进系统提示词或作为独立上下文。
dsh-user-preferences 的功能「偏好管理面板」：在 DSH 插件页面查看状态、编辑和保存全局偏好、切换启用状态与注入模式，并导入 Claude Code 或 Codex 规则文件。
dsh-user-preferences 的维护与更新元数据：活跃维护；距最后推送 38 天；提交数 1；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 62/100（置信度 low）。

dsh-user-preferences README · dsh-user-preferences：Replacement for `dsh-user-prompt`. Injects your standing preferences into every model request.
The host half avoids coupling to the settings service and handles optional-service and file errors without failing prompt assembly. A malformed package or missing hard dependency can still prevent activation.

dsh-user-preferences README · Files (edit in any editor; changes apply on the next request, no restart)：| File | Scope |
|---|---|
| `<dshHome>/preferences/global.md` | all sessions (`dshHome` = `$DSH_HOME` or `~/.dsh`) |
| `<project>/.dsh/preferences.md` | nearest to the session cwd; walks up, stops at the repo root (`.git`) or `~` |
| `<dshHome>/preferences/settings.json` | `{ "enabled": true, "mode": "section" \| "context" }`, overrides plugin config live |

dsh-user-preferences README · Modes：- `section` (default): merged into the system prompt (highest authority); `{{...}}` stays literal.
- `context`: separate user-role snapshot; every `{{` is defused so the renderer cannot throw.

dsh-user-preferences README · Startup resilience：- Only `systemPrompt` is a hard dependency; commands / connection are attached lazily via `ctx.inject`.
- It does not use the `settings` service; invalid settings-file values fall back at runtime.
- Prompt registrations and optional attachments are guarded, so an individual registration failure is logged instead of escaping `apply()`.
- Providers never throw: bad JSON, unreadable or oversized files, a directory in place of a file,
  a hostile agent shape all degrade to "inject nothing" plus one deduplicated log line.
- Transient read errors fall back to the last good content.
dsh-user-preferences README · Commands：`/preferences` shows the status. `/preferences path` prints the global file path.

dsh-user-preferences README · Install (desktop profile, local development)：1. Back up the profile's `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `cordis.patch.yml` and copy the old prompt to `<dshHome>/preferences/global.md`.
2. From the desktop profile directory, use the profile's pnpm runtime to add `link:D:/Programs/dsh-user-preferences`; include `dsh-user-preferences` in `dsh.profile.bundles` and remove `dsh-user-prompt` from both dependencies and bundles. Remove its `user-prompt` row from `cordis.patch.yml` without changing unrelated rows.
3. Reload the profile (or restart DSH if its HMR watcher is unavailable). Verify that the effective bundle composition contains `user-preferences` and not `user-prompt`, then confirm the Plugins → User preferences card loads and saves, and prompt assembly contains the migrated text. The generated `cordis.yml` can remain unchanged after a live HMR reconciliation; its timestamp alone does not prove whether the running Host reloaded.

dsh-user-preferences README · Install (desktop profile, local development)：The `link:` spec uses the local source directory. Keep that directory intact while installed. Revert the backed-up profile files and reinstall its dependencies to roll back; do not overwrite the migrated global preferences file.
